entry.title: Why embargoes matter for open source security
entry.content: Open source is built on a foundation of transparency, collaboration, and speed. We share code, we share ideas, and together, we build better software. But when it comes to discovering and patching security vulnerabilities, that standard model of immediate, public sharing has to temporarily shift. A security embargo is a temporary agreement to keep a software vulnerability private so that vendors and maintainers can create and release a security patch before malicious actors learn how to exploit
entry.dc:creator: Canonical Blog

entry.title: Merge Launchpad merge proposals with one click
entry.content: Maintainers can now merge changes (merge proposals) directly from the Launchpad UI. The new Request merge button is available to anyone with permission to push to the target branch. Launchpad enables it if the merge proposal has: An active status and an up-to-date diff No conflicts with the target branch Approval from the target repository owner, a member of its owner team, or designated review team Successfully completed any configured CI checks No unmerged prerequisite branches When you click
